summary_paragraph: A man with HIV/AIDS, chronic respiratory failure, tracheostomy, and functional quadriplegia was admitted with fever, tachycardia, and increased respiratory secretions. He was diagnosed with sepsis due to healthcare-associated pneumonia, likely from Klebsiella pneumoniae, and treated with IV cefepime and oral linezolid. His symptoms resolved, and labs improved. A concurrent Enterococcus faecium urinary finding was considered colonization but covered by linezolid. His home medications were continued, except citalopram, which was held due to interaction risk and scheduled for restart post-antibiotics. He was discharged to extended care with a plan to complete antibiotics and resume normal care.
